- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **136** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 744a0a3f1d501e18385d7d9b43aa1792db6e23e3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

This run read `content/docs` from `7b8b94968c63e6b34f34fcc06a642bd65f2bfff2` — the merge of head `f572bd4edeb350e80b93fca755f49ed367a8b596` into base `744a0a3f1d501e18385d7d9b43aa1792db6e23e3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 7b8b94968c63e6b34f34fcc06a642bd65f2bfff2 && git checkout 7b8b94968c63e6b34f34fcc06a642bd65f2bfff2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 744a0a3f1d501e18385d7d9b43aa1792db6e23e3 f572bd4edeb350e80b93fca755f49ed367a8b596 && git checkout -B drift-repro 744a0a3f1d501e18385d7d9b43aa1792db6e23e3 && git merge --no-ff f572bd4edeb350e80b93fca755f49ed367a8b596

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 744a0a3f1d501e18385d7d9b43aa1792db6e23e3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 744a0a3f1d501e18385d7d9b43aa1792db6e23e3` → pass the list as

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f572bd4edeb350e80b93fca755f49ed367a8b596`

Reviewed at 2026-09-22T02:26Z against the ruling's primary source (`objectstack-ai/objectui` `issuecomment-5749111840`, fetched, not carried), card #19579, the diff at the merge-base `0b4022b41c` (10 files, +321/−6 — reconciled), and the sibling at `origin/main` `0cf2d664`. Exit codes captured before any pipe; each zero paired with its radius and one known target outside it.

### ① Derived judgments

**The resolver is not a way around the schema — it is the instrument the ruling ordered.** This is the load-bearing decision and the PR's own framing undersells it. Ruling item 3, and card scope item 3 verbatim: 「if `FieldSchema` is a per-type union, `.default()` on each type's `scale`; **if it is flat, one exported resolver from spec that the `describe` names as the single source**」. I measured the shape rather than taking it: `FieldSchema` is a flat `strictObject` inside `lazySchema`, type applicability carried by `superRefine`, ⛔ not a per-type union. So the flat branch was already decided conditionally by the maintainer, and the dev's measurement satisfied its antecedent. The PR presents `yes` as its own re-judgement; the authority was upstream of it. Same answer, firmer ground.

**Leg 2 verified at the primary source, and it is real.** `packages/objectql/src/validation/record-validator.ts:789` is exactly `def.scale !== undefined &&` — the first conjunct of the `max_scale` gate (`&& Number.isInteger(def.scale) && def.scale >= 0`). A type-conditional `.overwrite()` materialising `0` would set `def.scale = 0` and arm the refusal at allowance `def.scale + 2` = **2** on a fraction-stored percent (`percentScaleOf(def) === 'fraction'`) and **0** on a whole-percent one. A percent field whose author declared nothing accepts any decimal count today; after materialisation it would refuse at 3+ places, or at all of them. That is a stored-data change bought for a display ruling, and one no author could read off their own metadata. The refusal of the idiomatic instrument stands on its own merits, independently of the ruling's flat branch.

**The `.overwrite()` precedent claim is true, and it cuts the same way.** `unique` and `deleteBehavior` are indeed type-conditionally materialised in `FieldSchema`'s `.overwrite()` tail (`field.zod.ts:2356`ff), so it was the idiomatic move. But the `deleteBehavior` #9689 comment sitting in that same tail records this exact class of mistake — 「NEVER materialize a default the schema itself would refuse as authored」, measured: four bare `master_detail` fields red the showcase build. Declining the instrument is consistent with the precedent immediately above it, not a departure from it. Nor was a better answer available in scope: materialising and then teaching the validator to tell authored from materialised is strictly larger, crosses into a second package's write path under a display ruling, and needs a provenance channel the parsed field does not carry — the same blindness the `unique` comment records (「can neither see `type` nor tell an omitted key from an authored `false`」). It is also the #11423 `precision` twin already carved off. The resolver is the minimum correct instrument.

**Non-materialisation is structurally conclusive, not merely pinned.** `field.zod.ts` changes exactly one line (+1/−1): the `.describe()` string. No `.default()`, no `.overwrite()` change ⇒ parse output is necessarily byte-identical and the bare-`percent` pin cannot be false. `authorable-defaults/data.json` carries no `scale` entry at all (0 hits, exit 1; control `unique` 2 hits, exit 0, file 124 lines) and is untouched, so ⛔ no `DEFAULT_CHANGES_BY_MAJOR` entry is owed. `authorable-surface/data.json` records `data/Field:scale` as a bare identity with no description text, so a describe rewrite cannot move it; untouched here (control: the same `git diff --name-only` grep matches `api-surface`/`export-origins`, which ARE touched — 2 hits, exit 0).

**The censuses genuinely do not license either type. Nothing that should have ridden was left behind.**
- `number` — **inconsistent, verified.** `packages/fields/src/index.tsx:772-773` resolves absence to no fixed width (`minimumFractionDigits: scale ?? 0`, `maximumFractionDigits: scale ?? 20`); `plugin-grid/src/useColumnSummary.ts:343` and `:401` and `plugin-dashboard/src/ObjectMetricWidget.tsx:229` resolve it to `0`. The load-bearing arm holds too: `packages/core/src/utils/number-display.ts:150-155` is `shouldGroupDisplayNumber(scale) => scale !== 0`, comment 「Only an explicitly declared scale of 0 is an ordinal. `undefined !== 0`」 — so `number ⇒ 0` would strip separators from every undeclared number field, printing `2026` for `2,026`. Correctly deferred.
- `currency` — the money faces do not read this key: `fields/src/currency.ts:25,41` memoises the ISO 4217 minor-unit width, `widgets/CurrencyField.tsx:15` takes authored `precision` or else the currency's own ISO 4217 digits, `index.tsx:484` says the non-whole width is the currency's minor-unit count. The one `2` that reads like a currency default is `GridField.tsx:321`, inside `computeRow`, rounding `evalArith(c.expr)` through `Number(v.toFixed(scale))` — the inline-grid COLUMN surface. **One precision:** for `currency` the reading is 「no face reads the key」, not 「faces disagree」. The PR's summary sentence 「Both came back inconsistent」 is looser than its own detailed table, which is exact. The ride condition (one *consistent* absent-value per type) fails either way, so the outcome is right — recorded so a later reader does not inherit the looser word.
- `percent` is consistent at `0` on five of six faces; the lone outlier is `widgets/PercentField.tsx:116` (`renderablePercentScale(typeof declaredScale === 'number' ? declaredScale : 2)`), whose own line 101 comment already reads 「An ABSENT `scale` keeps this widget's own 2.」 So `percent ⇒ 0` adopts the majority reading rather than inventing a number.

**Which `scale` — both claims check out.** At the merge-base, `field.zod.ts:1226` is `FieldSchema.scale` and `:931` is `InlineGridColumnSchema.scale`; both cited line numbers are exact. The grid schema's `type` enum is `text · number · currency · date · datetime · time · select · lookup · file` — ⛔ no `percent` member, so `percent ⇒ 0` has no landing there. And its key does round a platform-**computed** result: its own describe says so, its in-file comment names `computeRow` → `Number(v.toFixed(scale))`, and the consumer confirms it at `GridField.tsx:314-323`. Picking `FieldSchema.scale` and leaving the grid key alone is right.

**Ablation: the four reds are the right four.** Reproduced independently — resolver extracted verbatim, the 12 cases run at `percent: 0` and at `percent: 2`: **12 passed / 0 failed** at head, **4 failed / 8 passed** ablated, and the four are exactly the ones claimed — the ruled-value pin, the malformed-declaration door (its percent assertions fall through to the table), the numeric-family table pin, and the non-materialisation pin's resolver half. The two describe pins correctly stay green (the describe is a literal, not generated from the table), as do the declaration-wins, no-width, non-numeric, ceiling and round-trip cases. RED was the right prediction. The table pin's roster matches `NUMERIC_VALUE_TYPES` exactly (`number · currency · percent · rating · slider · progress · summary`) and fails in both directions, so `progress`/`summary` answering `undefined` is a recorded decision rather than a hole.

**The `.describe()` as author-facing prose — adequate, and it leads with the answer.** It opens 「Decimal places (integer 0-100). OMITTED on a `percent` field ⇒ 0 decimal places, so a stored 0.25 reads `25%` on every face; omitted on any OTHER numeric type declares NO fixed width…」 then names `resolveFieldScale` from `@objectstack/spec/data` as the single source. An author reading only the generated row gets the absent value, a worked example, the not-defaulted types, the declared-`0` distinction and where the answer lives — all before the pre-existing storage paragraph. That discharges the ③ facet and `docs/NORTH-STAR.md`:115 (verified in place). Cost, noted not filed: the row is now 1520 characters and the new text is prepended to an already-dense cell, so the reference page's `scale` entry is a wall. Nothing in it is false.

**The declared file-surface breach is exactly what was declared.** `api-surface/data.json` +2 = `FieldScaleMeta (interface)` and `resolveFieldScale (function)` in sorted position; `export-origins/data.json` +2 = the same two mapped to `src/data/field-scale.ts#…`. ⛔ Nothing else rode in. The three docs pages carry only the regenerated `scale` row (five rows across three pages), byte-equal to the new describe. No `json-schema.manifest/` change is owed — that artifact carries no describe text (probed: 5069 bytes, no describe prose, no new symbol).

### ② Semver level

**`minor` is correct and required.** The changeset grades `"@objectstack/spec": minor` and `packages/spec` is the only package the diff moves. Per `judgeLevel` in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `enforce` (exit 1) is 「the axis is CARRIED, moved packages graded `patch` and NONE of them graded `minor` or above」; with the axis carried by `yes` and spec at `minor`, `raised` is non-empty so `refusable` is false and no moved package is graded `patch` ⇒ verdict `clean`, exit 0. A `patch` here would have hit `enforce`. `Check Changeset` is green on this head.

**`Clause-②: yes (widening)` is right, and the GROUND holds — but not the claim's ground.** The claim argued `yes` from a `.default()` materialising a key; that ground is genuinely gone, since `field.zod.ts` moves one describe line and nothing materialises. The dev's limb is the correct one and I judged it from the diff: `data/index.ts` gains `export * from './field-scale'` and the published `@objectstack/spec/data` surface gains exactly two symbols. `.github/workflows/pr-automation.yml:753-755` — 「A purely additive widening of a published package's public surface (a new exported symbol on an `index`, a new accepted key or value) takes at least `minor`」, maintainer-ruled 2026-09-04, decision batch #35, on #15294 — is that act precisely, and `packages/spec/src/shared/scale-ceiling.ts:52-56` prices the identical act identically: 「a new export (`Clause-②: yes`, at least `minor`, and a contract-tier review)」. Doubly sourced, and well-formed under AGENTS.md:1077 (`yes` takes at least `minor`; `widening` is not the breaking arm).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **CI at review time: converged and fully green** — read at 2026-09-22T02:26Z, **39 check runs, 34 success, 5 skipped, 0 red, 0 pending**. All six `Test Core` shards, all four `Type Check` legs (`workspace` · `source gates` · `consumer gates` · `debt ledger`), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Build Core`, `Check Changeset`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` 1–3/3, `Dogfood Verify CLI`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Spec property liveness`, `Check Documentation Links`, `Build Docs` all success. Skipped: `Console Pin Gate` (nothing removed or renamed, so the pinned sibling cannot break), `Check PR Size`, `Auto Label`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`. The 17 gates outstanding at dispatch all landed green; nothing red, so nothing is a finding on this axis.
- **Both `NOT MEASURED` exit-3 declarations are honest — I reproduced both.** `node scripts/check-dual-build-cjs-loads.mjs` → **exit 3**, 「Run `pnpm build` first. ⛔ This is NOT a pass: nothing was measured」, naming 83 unbuilt export subpaths (1 of 31 `packages/*` has a `dist` in a fresh checkout). `node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs --re-measure` → **exit 3**, 「This is NOT a pass and NOT a finding: nothing was measured」. Both genuinely need a whole-workspace build, and CI covered both anyway — `Build Core` and `Type Check · debt ledger` are green on this head.
- **The ⛔ 「no `?? N`」 half is enforced by prose on this side only.** `resolveFieldScale` answers `undefined` for every type but `percent`, and the docblock forbids a caller's fallback on it — but nothing in the type system stops a consumer writing `resolveFieldScale(f) ?? 2`. The ruling assigns the five-site parity pin to objectui#9843, so this is correctly deferred, not missing; flagged so the consumer review knows the enforcement lives entirely on that side.
- **`number` and `currency` cards not yet filed.** No open `domain:spec` card names either (100 newest open `domain:spec` issues checked; only #19579 matches on scale/percent/currency/number). Card scope item 2 owes 「its own card with the readings」 for each. ⛔ Not a defect in this diff — the readings are recorded with exact sites and line numbers in the changeset, the `field-scale.ts` docblock and the PR body — but it is owed before they age out, and it is the seat's act, not the dev's.
- **objectui#9808's sunset is honoured, not bypassed.** The resolver returns an over-ceiling declared width verbatim (pinned: `scale: 101` → `101`) and adds ⛔ no second clamp policy; the clamping stays with the one consumer that rules on it (`PercentField.tsx:116`'s `renderablePercentScale`). That is what the ruling required.
- **No duplication with the existing sibling.** `data/percent-scale.ts` exports `PercentScale` · `PercentScaleFieldMeta` · `percentScaleOf` — storage magnitude (`fraction` vs `whole`), a different question from display width. No overlap, and the new module follows the same `…Meta`-interface-plus-resolver shape.
- **Still `draft: true`.** Flipping it, the label, and the merge are ⛔ not mine; `needs:contract-review` untouched by this act.
